In mathematics, '''Joyal's theorem''' is a theorem in [[homotopy theory]] that provides necessary and sufficient conditions for the solvability of a certain lifting problem involving [[simplicial set]]s. In particular, in [[higher category theory]], it proves the statement "an [[∞-groupoid]] is a [[Kan complex]]",<ref>{{harvnb|Rezk|2022||loc=35. Applications of the Joyal extension theorem}}</ref> which is a version of the [[homotopy hypothesis]].<ref>{{harvnb|Cisinski|2023|loc=Theorem 3.5.1.}}</ref>

The theorem was introduced by [[André Joyal]].

==Joyal's extension theorem==
Let <math>C</math> be [[quasicategory]] and let <math>u:X \rightarrow Y</math> be a [[morphism]] of <math>C</math>. The following conditions are equivalent:<ref>{{harvnb|Theorem 4.4.2.6 in Kerodon}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Rezk|2022||loc=34.2. Theorem}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|2009||loc=Proposition 1.2.4.3}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Joyal|2002|loc=Theorem 1.3}}</ref>

(1) The morphism <math>u</math> is an [[isomorphism]].

(2) Let <math>n \geq 2</math> and let <math>\sigma_0 : \Lambda^n_0 \to C</math> be a morphism of simplicial sets for which the initial edge

<math>\Delta^1 \cong N_{\bullet }( \{ 0 < 1\} ) \rightarrow \Lambda^n_ 0 \xrightarrow {\sigma _0} C</math>

is equal to <math>u</math>. Then <math>\sigma_0</math> can be extended to an [[Kan fibration#Definition of the standard n-simplex|''n''-simplex]] <math>\sigma : \Delta^n \to C</math>.

(3) Let <math>n \geq 2</math> and let <math>\sigma_0 : \Lambda^n_n \rightarrow C</math> be a morphism of simplicial sets for which the initial edge

<math>\Delta^1 \cong N_{\bullet }( \{ n-1 < n\} ) \rightarrow \Lambda^n_ n \xrightarrow {\sigma _0} C</math>

is equal to <math>u</math>. Then <math>\sigma_0</math> can be extended to an ''n''-simplex <math>\sigma : \Delta^n \to C</math>.

==Joyal's lifting theorem==
Let <math>p: C \rightarrow D</math> be an [[inner fibration]] (Joyal used mid-fibration<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|2009||page=xiv}}</ref>) between quasicategories, and let <math>f  \in C_1</math> be an edge such that <math>p (f)</math> is an isomorphism in <math>D</math>. The following are equivalent:<ref>{{harvnb|Rezk|2022|loc=34.17. Theorem (Joyal lifting).}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Haugseng|loc=Theorem 5.3.1.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Kapulkin|Voevodsky|2020|loc=Theorem 2.10}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Land|2021|loc=Theorem. 2.1.8}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Joyal|2002|loc=Theorem 2.2}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Joyal|2008|loc=Theorem 6.13}}</ref>

(1) The edge <math>f</math> is an isomorphism in <math>C</math>.

(2) For all <math>n \geq 2</math>, every diagram of the form

admits a [[Lift (mathematics)|lift]].

(3) For all <math>n \geq 2</math>, every diagram of the form

admits a lift.
